arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Sady argued the phrase term of imprisonment appears three times in the statute.
He stated the first two uses mean the sentence imposed.
Mr. Wall argued the statute language tracks the Bureau's practice.
He noted Justice Breyer described the Bureau's method correctly.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks how to interpret the phrase term of imprisonment in the federal good time statute. the sides that brought the case argue it means the sentence imposed by the court. the opposing sides argue it means the actual time served. The lower court ruled against the sides that brought the case. The Supreme Court will decide which interpretation applies.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case want the Court to hold that the sentence ends on the date of the imposed term.
the opposing sides want the Court to hold that the sentence ends after the full time served.
